name: Malakir Rebirth // Malakir Mire
oracle_text: Choose target creature. You lose 2 life. Until end of turn, that creature gains "When this creature dies, return it to the battlefield tapped under its owner's control."
blocked_sentences: Choose target creature. You lose 2 life. Until end of turn, that creature gains "When this creature dies, return it to the battlefield tapped under its owner's control."

needs.what: modal double-faced cards: a second, separately playable face with its own cost and type line, chosen as the card is played. Here the front is an Instant and the back is a Land, so the back must go down the land-drop path (no stack, consumes the land drop) while the front is cast normally.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: docs/rules-coverage.md:52 states the position outright -- transforming DFCs are modelled but "a back face here is a face, not a second castable card" -- and :157 lists modal double-faced cards as not implemented. `back_face` exists but only ever describes the face a permanent shows after transforming; nothing offers it as a way to play the card. The authoring pipeline emits exactly one card entry per answer file (`collect_answers` reads `answer["card"]` as a single dict), and a double-faced card is two card entries linked by `back_face`. Gate 3 compounds it: `collect_answers` looks the oracle text up by the payload's name, and a front face authored under its own name misses the catalog's joined "A // B" row. The repo's existing two-faced cards (bloodline_keeper / lord_of_lineage) are hand-written in data/cards/ for exactly this reason.
